defaultActivation: Ordinary owned local Pipeline9 and its worker batch enable contact refinement when their existing full-context priorityDagSearch policy is enabled. Projected 9net inputs keep the original MultiHead3 solver.
replacedWork: MultiHead3 keeps its inherited ViaPossibilitiesSolver2 discrete seeds and seed deduplication. Continuous XY refinement uses a coupled elastic halfspace QP instead of optimized2 endpoint, segment and via exponential force sweeps.
mechanism: Sweep conservative XY envelopes expanded by copper radius, clearance and sqrt(2) times the endpoint trust-box radius.
Retain only potentially active contacts; exact pair distance omission uses the sum of the two whole-segment motion bounds.
A fixed unit separating normal supplies every endpoint-pair inequality, a sufficient full-segment separation certificate.
Hildreth dual coordinate updates minimize displacement plus quadratic contact slack. Trust and boundary rows have no slack.
Accepted proposals decrease exact whole-primitive clearance residuals; rejected proposals restore coordinates and change a bounded explicit side/trust choice.
Only actual zero-violation physical geometry can finish: route/trace/via/pad/hole/board checks plus owner-independent configured drill spacing.
Through vias occupy the full physical layer stack; grow/shrink coordinates scale all modeled physical dimensions and are unscaled for final board validation.

limits.workAccounting: New geometry collection, normal/row assembly, QP preprocessing/updates/witness checks and final validation consume one shared cap. The external physical checker receives a conservative quadratic primitive reservation. The inherited discrete seed setup remains unchanged, including its existing min(2000, factorial(connectionCount)) bound; contactInheritedSeedSetups and contactRetainedSeeds expose this separately.
limits.qpSweepCap: A nonstationary bounded QP proposal is exported only with a checked hard-row witness and explicit remaining slack. It never constitutes route acceptance or an infeasibility proof.

limitations: The continuous backend cannot create missing vias or change layer topology/homotopy. Exhaustion is explicit unknown, never UNSAT, and does not invoke the old force backend.
Fixed-obstacle disks conservatively enclose rectangular/rotated geometry for optimization; exact board validation can accept a physically valid route before those proxy contacts clear.
Board-outline violations not represented by the local contact model are rejected by final physical validation rather than treated as solved.
No measured speedup is claimed; central serial sample replay decides whether contact reduction exceeds model and validation overhead.
